4. Mr. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party, No 1 contends that the petitioner should seek her remedy through Civil Court as contemplated under Sub- section (2) of section 522 Cr. P. C. in this connection Mr. Fazlul Karim has referred the case of Narayan Govinda Ps. Visaji 23 I.L.R. page 494 wherein the view has been taken that the case of a proper order third person could not be affected, if they are, the order is not thereby necessarily invalid: Clause (2) Or the section gives the remedy by Civil SO. Mr. Fazlul Karim contends that possession one petitioner Ambia Khatun was not found by any court and as such it will not be proper to restore possession to her. In this connection Mr. Fazlul Karim has referred to the case of Abdul. Karim Vs. The Crown reported in P.L.D. 1950. Lahore, page 154 wherein the view has been taken that no logical consideration compel the court to put into possession of any immovable property a person who was convicted an offence involving use or show of criminal force or criminal intimidation in respect of shelf properly and who was deprived of its possession following such conviction, by an order under section 522, Criminal Procedure Code, merely section 522, Criminal Procedure Code, merely by reason of such person having been acquitted of the offence. 

 6. Mr. Salek, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner contends before me that on acquittal of the accused persons from the charge under section 448 B.P.C., the order passed by the learned Magistrate under section 522 Cr.P.C. restoring possession to O.P. No. 1 Raja Mia must go and that the order may be passed to put the persons in possession from whom the possession was taken. From the case reported in 20 D.L.R. page 1108 it will appear that the case reported in P.L.D. 1950 Lahore 154 is the leading case on the point which was reed on, in the case reported in 20 D.L.R. page 1108 also. In the case reported in P.L.D. 1950 Lahore, 154 the view has been taken, as I have already observed, that the court is not bound to restore possession to a convicted person merely because of his subsequent acquittal.
